relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a child with genetically confirmed arterial tortuosity syndrome: 'Whole exome sequencing revealed one likely pathogenic single nucleotide variant and one pathogenic deletion in SLC2A10 gene'.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; JSON assembled by a short Python script from hand-chosen values and spans. One in-scope person (unnamed single patient; 'proband' is a role word, so label 'patient'). The paper prints no description of either SLC2A10 variant, so two variant rows were kept with variant_original_string 'not reported'; variant type left 'not reported' because 'single nucleotide variant' and 'deletion' do not map unambiguously to the enum (SNV class unknown; deletion size unknown); zygosity/phase not stated (no parental testing: parents declined), so 'not reported' rather than compound heterozygous. The only age given is 'A 5-year-old male was presented to the hospital' (age at presentation); the paper does not state the age at which ATS was diagnosed or when WES was done, nor the age at the 1-year follow-up, so all age fields are 'not reported'. 'Slightly deformed chest' is not specified as pectus, so the pectus checklist item is 'not reported'. Normal blood pressure at presentation recorded as excluded elevated blood pressure / systemic hypertension (D-27). Dysphagia is observed before surgery and reported absent one year after surgery; both rows emitted (temporal change, not a contradiction; dysphagia is not a checklist item). No internal contradictions found. Ethnicity/country of the patient not stated (only the authors' Lithuanian affiliation).

treatment_summary.value: oral amoxicillin; metoprolol and enalapril (continued); surgical repair via median sternotomy on cardiopulmonary bypass: aneurysm resected, direct anastomosis between aortic root and proximal aortic arch, external 20 mm vascular graft wrap
span: The patient was hospitalised and started on oral amoxicillin.
Metoprolol and enalapril were prescribed in an attempt to slow the aortic growth rate.
The surgery was performed via median sternotomy using cardiopulmonary bypass.

the aneurysm was resected at the level of the proximal aortic arch. A direct anastomosis between the aortic root and the proximal aortic arch was made. A knitted 20 mm vascular graft was wrapped around the reconstructed part externally
The patient continues to use metoprolol and enalapril.
